items.stem: In DDD, what is the primary responsibility of an aggregate root?

options.text: To enforce the invariants of the whole aggregate and be the only entry point for changes
options.rationale: Correct: the aggregate root guards consistency and is the single channel for modifying the aggregate.

options.text: To map directly to a single database table
options.rationale: An aggregate may span several tables; persistence shape is not its defining role.

options.text: To expose all child entities for direct external modification
options.rationale: Direct external modification of children bypasses invariant protection and is discouraged.

options.text: To hold only query logic for reporting
options.rationale: Reporting/query concerns belong to the read side in CQRS, not the aggregate root.

items.explanation: Correct: the aggregate root guards consistency and is the single channel for modifying the aggregate.

items.stem: Select TWO statements that correctly describe a simplified CQRS approach as used in the .NET microservices guidance.

options.text: Queries are side-effect free and can use a simpler read model
options.rationale: Correct: queries are idempotent and may use a dedicated read model.

options.text: Commands change state and are a good place to apply DDD patterns
options.rationale: Correct: the transactional write side benefits from DDD modeling.

options.text: CQRS always mandates separate read and write databases
options.rationale: A simplified CQRS can use the same database for both sides.

options.text: Queries should mutate aggregates to stay consistent
options.rationale: Queries must not change state; that would violate CQRS.

options.text: Commands and queries must share one identical model
options.rationale: CQRS deliberately allows different models for reads and writes.

items.explanation: Correct: queries are idempotent and may use a dedicated read model.

items.stem: You must propagate a side effect across two aggregates after an order starts, favoring scalability and fewer database locks. What approach fits the DDD guidance best?

options.text: Raise a domain event and use eventual consistency between the aggregates
options.rationale: Correct: domain events with eventual consistency reduce lock contention across aggregates.

options.text: Update both aggregates inside one large transaction by default
options.rationale: A single transaction across aggregates increases locking and is discouraged as a default.

options.text: Let one aggregate directly navigate and mutate the other
options.rationale: Direct navigation and mutation across aggregates breaks boundaries and invariants.

options.text: Perform the side effect in a read query handler
options.rationale: Query handlers must remain side-effect free.

items.explanation: Correct: domain events with eventual consistency reduce lock contention across aggregates.
